definitions.explanation: The curved path of a celestial body or spacecraft around another object due to gravity.
The rails on which trains or trams run.
Figuratively, the expected or proper course of action or development.

notes:
USAGE: {軌道|きどう} has both literal (astronomy/transportation) and figurative uses.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {軌道|きどう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{乗|の}る→乗る：00511_noru⟧ (to get into orbit; to get on track)
- {軌道|きどう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{乗|の}せる→乗せる：01972_noseru⟧ (to put into orbit; to set on the right track)
- {軌道|きどう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{外|はず}れる→外れる：02395_hazureru⟧ (to go off orbit/track)
- {軌道|きどう}⟦{修正|しゅうせい}→修正：03210_shuusei⟧ (course correction)

SCIENTIFIC TERMS:
- ⟦{円軌道|えんきどう}→円軌道：29617_enkidou⟧ - circular orbit
- ⟦{楕円軌道|だえんきどう}→楕円軌道：29618_daenkidou⟧ - elliptical orbit
- ⟦{静止軌道|せいしきどう}→静止軌道：29619_seishikidou⟧ - geostationary orbit

IDIOMATIC EXPRESSION: {軌道|きどう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{乗|の}る→乗る：00511_noru⟧ is frequently used figuratively to mean that a project, business, or effort has reached a stable, successful state.
